explainBack.question: Why could Nvidia's deal with Groq draw competition attention even though Nvidia never bought Groq?
explainBack.answer: Because two things reportedly moved even without ownership changing hands: Nvidia gained a non-exclusive licence — permission to use Groq's inference technology, which does not by itself stop Groq from using or licensing it — and Groq's founder, president and other team members joined Nvidia while Groq stayed independent with GroqCloud continuing. Reuters, citing the New York Times and two people familiar with the matter, reported the Justice Department is asking whether the agreement was structured to avoid antitrust scrutiny and sent a formal request for information. That is an inquiry — a set of questions — not a finding; what the licence and hires actually changed in practice remains unanswered by the reporting.
explainBack.expectedEvidence: A correct answer must name both moving parts (licence and senior hires), retain Groq's continued independence, preserve the Reuters/NYT attribution chain, and explicitly stop at inquiry-not-finding without supplying legal classification or market effects.
explainBack.assessment: The article's own material in P002–P006 fully supports this answer in ordinary language; the mechanism is complete and the evidence limits survive the retelling, so explain-back passes.

unseenTransfer.scenario: Invented scenario: a dominant global mapping-software company signs a non-exclusive licence to use a small navigation startup's real-time traffic-prediction technology, and the startup's founder and chief engineer join the larger company; the startup announces it remains an independent business and its consumer app will keep running. A national newspaper later reports, citing unnamed people familiar with the matter, that a competition authority has opened an inquiry and requested information.
unseenTransfer.question: Using the article's mechanism, what should a careful reader conclude is stipulated, what is open, and why might such a deal draw competition attention without any acquisition?
unseenTransfer.answer: Stipulated by the scenario: the non-exclusive licence, the two senior hires, the startup's continued independence, and a reported inquiry with an information request. Open questions: what access to the technology and the movement of experienced people actually changed in practice, whether the deal's structure was chosen for any particular reason, and what, if anything, the authority will conclude. The same pattern as the article applies — technology access plus people movement can prompt a competition question even when the smaller company is not bought — but the reported inquiry is only a set of questions. I do not supply any legal classification, jurisdictional threshold, market effect or outcome, because neither the article's mechanism nor the scenario's stipulated facts establish them.
unseenTransfer.expectedEvidence: A sound transfer keeps stipulated facts separate from open questions, reuses the licence-plus-hires mechanism from P004–P005, and preserves the inquiry-versus-finding boundary from P003 and P006 without inventing outcomes.
unseenTransfer.assessment: The mechanism transfers cleanly to this new industry with all evidence limits intact, which demonstrates the article teaches a genuinely portable distinction rather than a one-off fact.
